Event Overview

The U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) carried out military strikes against Iran-backed armed groups inside Iraq, stating that these groups pose a direct threat to the United States and Saudi Arabia. Simply put: the U.S. got angry and went straight after Iran’s underlings. This isn’t only a Middle East issue—global risk assets will be affected, and the crypto market is likely to be hit first.

In-Depth Analysis

Why is this news important?

Brothers and sisters, this isn’t as simple as firing a couple of shots.

First layer of logic: The Middle East situation has long been a “powder keg” for global financial markets. This time, the U.S. directly targeted Iran-linked forces, showing that the Biden administration chose a hardline approach in the face of security threats—leaving less room for diplomatic negotiations. If Iran chooses retaliation, oil supply near the Strait of Hormuz could be disrupted, oil prices could spike, inflation expectations would return, and the timeline for Fed rate cuts would likely be pushed back.

Second layer of logic: For the crypto market, the impact of geopolitical conflict cuts both ways. In the short term, panic will cause some capital to pull out of risk assets, and BTC and ETH could both get hammered. But in the medium term, every geopolitical crisis makes more people realize that you need an asset that won’t be frozen by any government and won’t be restricted by banks. During the 2022 Russia–Ukraine conflict, BTC was the best example.

Third layer of logic: Now BTC is at $63,951 and ETH is at $1,919—both are already in relatively sensitive ranges where price action can be easily amplified. When market sentiment shifts toward safe-haven behavior, gold and BTC often move up together.

Market Impact

In the short term, right after the airstrike news breaks, the market’s first reaction is likely panic. BTC may quickly dip around $63,951 and run a stop-hunt spike downward. ETH will likely follow, and the $1,919 level may not hold against the first wave of selling pressure.

But honestly: if Iran’s response is only verbal condemnation, with no substantive military retaliation, then this bearish factor is just a paper tiger. BTC could rebound quickly, and even break above the current consolidation range. The market will realize that the conflict hasn’t escalated, panic fades, and the previously sidelined capital comes back.

Looking back at April 2024, when Iran directly launched missile strikes at Israel, BTC dropped sharply below $60,000 in the short term—but regained the lost ground in less than a week. The impact of geopolitical conflict on BTC is increasingly looking like a “V-shaped reversal” script.

ETH’s recent performance has been weaker than BTC: it’s up only about 1.95% over 24 hours. If this safe-haven sentiment fades, ETH will very likely catch up.

Zelensky and Netanyahu Met Up in Washington! Geopolitical Power Game Escalates—Can BTC at $64,040 Hold Up?

Event Overview

To put it simply, two big bosses from two different fronts both came to Washington to meet with Trump. Zelensky wants military aid to stay alive, while Netanyahu wants the U.S. to back his Middle East policy. With two hot spots involving major conflicts laid on the table at the same time, how well the talks go will directly shape where global risk-hedging sentiment flows. For the crypto market, this kind of high-level political meeting is never a small matter—safe-haven buying could push BTC higher, but a breakdown in negotiations could also trigger panic selling.

In-Depth Interpretation

Why is this news important?

Honestly, the timing of this meeting is extremely delicate. The Russia-Ukraine war has been going on for nearly three years. Just after the Middle East situation seemed to calm down, it could flare up again at any moment. With the parties to both conflicts showing up in Washington simultaneously, the market receives a clear signal: geopolitical risk is far from over.

The core issue is Trump’s stance. He previously claimed he would end the Russia-Ukraine war within “24 hours,” but everyone knows that kind of promise can’t be fulfilled. If the signal from this meeting is “keep fighting,” then global funds will continue to move into safe-haven assets. If a de-escalation signal is released, risk assets could breathe a little.

Looking at the current cycle, BTC is consolidating around $64,040. In the past 24 hours, it’s only up 0.44%. ETH is even worse: $1,923.67 is barely up 1.87% and still struggling. The market itself is waiting for a catalyst, and geopolitics is precisely the most uncontrollable variable. In plain terms, the market doesn’t fear rate hikes or regulation as much as it fears a black-swan-level escalation of geopolitical conflict.

From a capital-flow perspective, both institutions and retail investors are in a wait-and-see mode. They don’t dare go heavily long, and they don’t dare fully exit. At times like this, a single sentence—or even one facial expression—in Washington can determine the direction of billions of dollars.

Market Impact

First, in the short term, the meeting itself is uncertainty, and uncertainty suppresses market sentiment. BTC at $64,040 is neither strong nor weak. There’s no catalyst above, while below there’s support—but it may not hold under panic. ETH at $1,923.67 is even more awkward; it hasn’t reclaimed $2,000. If geopolitical headlines worsen, ETH will likely fall far more aggressively than BTC.

In the medium term, you need to see the actual results of the meeting. If there are signs of de-escalation—even if it’s only talk—risk assets may see a bounce. But if talks fail or more hardline statements appear, safe-haven funds will accelerate into gold and BTC, which could ironically become a catalyst for BTC.

Historical reference is clear: whenever major geopolitical events erupt, BTC usually dips in the short term, but afterward it often trades independently and forms its own momentum. Last year, when the Middle East situation tightened, BTC briefly probed lower and then rebounded quickly. This year, when the Russia-Ukraine situation escalated, it looked similar. The key difference this time is that it’s not the conflict itself that matters most, but diplomatic mediation—which is more indirect and more gradual.

Trading Approach

🎯 Impact Forecast
- Coins: BTC / ETH
- Direction: Neutral to slightly bearish short-term📉. Geopolitical uncertainty suppresses upside potential.
- Duration: BTC 12 hours / ETH 24 hours

💡 My take: Don’t rush to add to positions in the short term. Around BTC $64,040, long-versus-short battles are intense. If it breaks below the $63,000 support level, the next level to watch is the $60,000 round-number zone. ETH is more fragile: $1,900 is the line in the sand—if it breaks, it’s likely heading straight to $1,800. If you already have a position, setting a stop-loss is more important than anything. Wait for the meeting outcome before deciding your direction—don’t sprint too early.

In-depth analysis

Why is this news important?

To put it bluntly: a futures open-interest figure hitting an all-time high is absolutely not an ordinary signal.

The core contradiction is that the market’s disagreement about the Fed’s next move has reached an extreme. Inflation data shows signs of cooling, and expectations for rate cuts have been heating up. But the jobs market is still stubbornly strong, and Powell has every reason to keep rates high. This “caught between both sides” situation forces institutional funds to lay out aggressively in the futures market—whether the move is up or down is secondary; first they put the chips on the table.

Viewed within the industry cycle, this moment is even more crucial. BTC has been ranging around $64,042 for a while and still hasn’t chosen a direction. There’s also a point that’s easy to overlook: open interest at this scale can’t be driven by retail traders at all. This indicates that traditional big institutions are taking this decision extremely seriously. The crypto market is becoming more deeply tied to macro dynamics. Back then, BTC used to look at its own ecosystem—now it has to look at Powell’s face.

Impact on the market

In the short term, when the rate decision is announced, prices may “snap” upward like a slingshot. The higher the open interest, the stronger the impact of concentrated liquidations. To be honest, in the hours before and after the decision, the battle between longs and shorts will be extremely brutal, and liquidation volumes are likely to spike.

The mid-term trend is what really matters. Based on historical experience, a combination of high open interest and low volatility is often a sign of an approaching turning point. 📰 美联储决议前夜！期货持仓创历史新高，BTC $64,042要变盘？

事件概述

老铁们，这事不简单。美联储马上要开利率决议会议，华尔街那帮大资金在期货市场疯狂堆筹码，持仓量直接干到了历史最高纪录。什么意思？所有人都在赌一个大波动要来。BTC现在$64,042，ETH报$1,923，表面上风平浪静，底下全是暗流涌动。

深度解读

为什么这条新闻重要？

说白了，期货持仓量创历史新高，这绝对不是普通信号。

核心矛盾在于：市场对美联储下一步的分歧已经到了极点。通胀数据有降温迹象，降息预期一直在升温；但就业市场还硬得很，鲍威尔完全有理由继续维持高利率。这种两头堵的局面，逼着机构资金在期货市场上疯狂布局——涨跌先不管，先把筹码推上桌。

放在行业周期里看，这个节点更关键。BTC在$64,042附近横了有一阵了，迟迟选不出方向。ETH跌到$1,923，距离前高已经回撤不少。整个市场就像一根压到极限的弹簧，期货高持仓就是蓄积的势能，等的就是一个催化剂把它引爆。

还有个容易被忽略的点：这种级别的持仓量，散户根本推不出来。说明传统大资金对这次决议的态度极其认真，加密市场跟宏观的绑定越来越深了。以前BTC看自己生态的脸色，现在得看鲍威尔的脸色。

短期来看，利率决议公布那一刻，价格会像弹弓一样弹出去。持仓量越高，集中平仓的冲击力越猛。如果美联储释放鸽派信号，BTC可能直接拉升突破；要是偏鹰，砸盘速度也不会客气。讲真，决议前后那几小时，多空博弈会非常惨烈，爆仓量大概率会飙升。

中期趋势才是真正要关注的。从历史经验看，高持仓量+低波动率的组合，往往是变盘前兆。2023年3月硅谷银行暴雷前，也是类似的高持仓状态，结果反而成了BTC启动大涨的起点。所以高持仓本身不是坏事，关键看催化剂往哪个方向打。

资金面上，如果决议偏鸽，增量资金入场会加速，BTC和ETH都有反弹空间。如果偏鹰，短期杠杆被清洗一波也不是坏事，挤完泡沫更健康。

The logic chain in this incident is pretty clear:
Iranian missile attack → U.S. military response preparation → Strait of Hormuz passage risk spikes → global oil price expectations jump → panic in traditional markets → funds search for a safe-haven exit.

Looking at the current cycle, BTC at the $63,783 level is actually quite delicate. The broader market has just gone through a volatility washout; retail sentiment is fragile, and institutional money is watching from the sidelines. Then a geopolitical “black swan” hits suddenly. In the short term, it can trigger panic selling, but in the medium term it may become a catalyst for the crypto market.

Why? Because 2024 is different from before. BTC now has ETF channels—Wall Street money can flow in via an “all-you-can-eat” setup. Once traditional markets start to wobble due to a surge in oil prices, some smarter funds may treat BTC like digital gold for allocation. The last time Iran and Israel went at each other, BTC dipped briefly, then bounced back to V-shape within a few days.

Market impact

In the short term, when the news first breaks, the market’s first reaction will definitely be panic. ETH is currently at $1,916.64 and is down 1.41% over the past 24 hours, which suggests sentiment is already weak. Although BTC is basically flat over the last 24 hours at $63,783.03, that calm masks fragile liquidity. A slightly larger sell order could easily punch a hole in the price.

But I believe this is a move with a higher probability of a “fake drop.” The logic is simple:

First, geopolitical conflict’s impact on the crypto market is becoming shorter-lived. Funds have learned the “sell first, buy back later” playbook. Panic sellers are just the ammunition for others to step in and buy.

Second, if the Strait of Hormuz truly gets hit, a surge in oil would push inflation expectations higher. The market may start betting again that the Fed will have to choose between inflation and recession. This kind of uncertainty is actually favorable for assets like BTC with a fixed supply.

Third, ETH’s weakness lately is more about its own selling pressure and Layer2 diversion issues, not geopolitics. If BTC stabilizes and rebounds on the safe-haven narrative, ETH may move up too, but its upside elasticity may be weaker than BTC’s.

For historical reference: during the Iran–U.S. conflict in January 2020, BTC fell from $7,200 to $6,400 in the short term, then regained ground within a week and continued higher. The Strait of Hormuz is back on the table again. This time, Iran is putting out a tough statement: it plans to impose a transit ban on countries that have used Iranian frozen assets. Put simply: if you dare to use the money you froze of mine, then I dare to block the throat of your oil shipments.

This tactic isn’t new, but the timing is extremely sensitive. With BTC at $63,891 (down 1.66% in 24 hours) and ETH at $1,917, the market was already digesting selling pressure. As soon as geopolitical risk rears its head, sentiment instantly gets poured gasoline.

Event Overview

Iran warns it may shut off passage rights through the Strait of Hormuz to specific countries—those that have used Iranian frozen assets. About 20% of the world’s oil flows through this strait each day. If it is truly blocked, oil prices would jump immediately, and global risk assets would fall first out of caution.

However, here’s the counterintuitive logic: when traditional markets panic, the crypto market may temporarily decline in tandem—but the safe-haven narrative for BTC could be activated at the same time. The more chaotic the Middle East gets, the easier it is to tell the “digital gold” story.

In-Depth Analysis

Why is this news important?

Let’s be honest: Iran has played the Hormuz card more than ten times, and every time it was thunder with little rain. The difference this time is the—background is worse.

First, the frozen Iranian assets are actually being used. This isn’t just verbal intimidation—it’s real money being taken away. Iran can’t save face, neither in optics nor substance. From an industry cycle perspective, the market is currently in the post–BTC halving consolidation phase, where narratives are scarce and capital is watching. Any geopolitical-level catalyst could be amplified in interpretation.

Second, Iran’s settlement ties with Russia and China are increasingly dependent on crypto assets. If Iran is truly pushed into a corner, it can’t be ruled out that it accelerates the use of USDT and other cryptocurrencies to route around sanctions. For the entire crypto market, this is actually a long-term liquidity tailwind.

Third, if the Fear & Greed Index is in a low range, geopolitical conflicts often act as the trigger for a sentiment reversal. A historical pattern: in January 2020, during the US-Iran conflict, BTC initially plunged from $6,900 to $6,800, but rebounded within two weeks and broke above $8,000. The window for panic buying often appears right when everyone is shouting “run.”

Market Impact

In the short term, BTC at the $63,891 level is already caught in a tug-of-war between bulls and bears. If Iran stirs things up, the first reaction is likely to be a hit to safe-haven sentiment—leading to a drop first. A surge in crude oil would also stoke inflation expectations, and the Fed rate-cut narrative becomes even more complicated.

But to put it plainly, this kind of drop is likely a “fake dive.” The causal chain from geopolitics to crypto is: short-term panic selling → liquidity squeeze → capital exits high-risk assets → then realizing the scarcity narrative of BTC is actually worth more → capital returns.

ETH at $1,917 is more fragile. It is already down 1.44% over the past 24 hours. If panic sentiment spreads, ETH could test the lows ahead of BTC. But when it rebounds, ETH often rebounds more aggressively—when leverage washouts get harsher, upside elasticity tends to increase.

On the medium term, if the Strait of Hormuz truly faces substantial disruption, oil prices would spike → inflation expectations rise → rate cuts by the Fed are delayed → that line is bearish for risk assets. But the other line is: Iran accelerates crypto-based settlements → on-chain activity surges → the market starts trading the “crypto routes around sanctions” narrative again. These two lines would compete simultaneously, and volatility would be cranked up.

Trading Outlook

🎯 Impact Forecast

Friends who have followed me for a relatively long time should know that I started paying close attention to the development of on-chain infrastructure quite early, and I also began discussing—fairly early on—the long-term potential of areas such as DEX and RWA in the long-term integration of traditional finance. Today’s Hype and the trend of a coin-stock merger were arguments I wrote down three years ago, but back then not many people believed them.

At the time, I judged that a Bitcoin spot ETF would most likely go through. One of the key logics was that the ETF would not drain liquidity from the crypto market. Instead, it would become an important bridge connecting traditional capital and the crypto market.

Many people worry that money will all run to trade U.S. stocks, and that the crypto world will become increasingly short of liquidity.

But I’ve always believed that what truly happens is not replacement of capital, but market integration.

When Wall Street actively embraces blockchain, it means more capital, more institutions, and more regulatory frameworks will gradually enter this space. As foundational infrastructure such as stablecoins, RWA, on-chain settlement, on-chain clearing, and DEX continues to mature, liquidity sources for the crypto market will become more diverse—not increasingly scarce.

Today’s crypto market still has a strong wild-growth character. Regulation, institutions, and the structure of participants are still being refined. As governments, regulators, and financial institutions continue to participate, the industry may lose some disorderly upside, but it will also gain a more mature and stable development environment.

In the past, the crypto market talked about the narrative of Bitcoin.

In the future, the crypto market will talk about the narrative of integrating blockchain technology with the traditional financial system.

quoteContent.body:
难道加密资产的投资者，都跑去炒美股了？

今年市场确实出现了一个比较明显的现象：越来越多加密资金开始关注 RWA，部分链上流动性因此受到抑制。

但不少人既不真正理解加密资产，也不真正理解股票市场，只是跟着热点不断切换赛道。

股市和币市本质上是两套完全不同的体系。

股票市场背后是企业经营、盈利能力和现金流，加密资产更多依赖区块链网络、协议价值、链上经济以及去中心化基础设施的发展。两者可以融合，但并不会因此失去各自的底层逻辑。

更值得关注的是，这轮融合并不是币圈主动拥抱华尔街，而是华尔街主动寻求与加密市场融合。无论是稳定币、RWA、资产代币化，还是链上结算、托管、清算体系，本质上都是传统金融借助区块链基础设施提升效率。

加密资产过去很多年，有许多人莫名其妙富有，也会随着技术平替，莫名其妙失去财富。

技术的发展，正在逐渐抹平许多依赖信息差和运气获得的超额收益。

对于没有完成思维转变的加密巨鲸而言，当市场进入币股融合时代，过去依靠单一市场积累的经验正在快速失效。如果仍然沿用牛市的惯性思维，在股票和加密市场之间频繁切换，本质上就像在裸奔。

从链上数据来看，近几个月不少活跃巨鲸都在股票与加密资产之间反复切换仓位，部分账户出现了较大的资产回撤。一些人会逐渐退出市场，也有人会在这一轮洗牌中失去过去积累的大部分优势。

Have crypto investors all gone to trade U.S. stocks?

This year, there’s definitely been a fairly clear trend: more and more crypto capital has started paying attention to RWA, and some on-chain liquidity has therefore been constrained.

But many people neither truly understand crypto assets nor the stock market—they just keep chasing the latest hot topic and constantly switch tracks.

In essence, the stock market and the crypto market are two completely different systems.

Behind the stock market are a company’s operations, profitability, and cash flow. Crypto assets rely more on blockchain networks, the value of protocols, on-chain economics, and the development of decentralized infrastructure. The two can be integrated, but they won’t lose their underlying logic.

What’s more worth关注 is that this round of integration is not the crypto world主动 embracing Wall Street; it’s Wall Street actively seeking integration with the crypto market. Whether it’s stablecoins, RWA, or tokenization of assets—whether it’s on-chain settlement, custody, or clearing systems—at bottom, it’s traditional finance using blockchain infrastructure to improve efficiency.

Over many years, crypto assets have made many people inexplicably rich, and as technology “replaces” them, they can just as inexplicably lose their wealth.

Technological progress is gradually erasing a large portion of the excess returns that once came from information asymmetry and luck.

For crypto “whales” that haven’t completed a mental shift, when the market enters the era of crypto-stock convergence, experience accumulated from relying on a single market is quickly becoming invalid. If people still cling to the momentum mindset of a bull market and frequently switch between stocks and crypto markets, in essence it’s like running around buck naked.

From on-chain data, in the past few months many active whales have repeatedly rotated positions between stocks and crypto assets, and some accounts have seen significant asset drawdowns. Over many years, crypto assets have made many people inexplicably rich, and as technology “replaces” them, they can just as inexplicably lose their wealth.

Announcing the shutdown isn’t because it’s a bear market—it’s a vulnerability. In the same hour, buying 73 million of Ethereum pushed the holdings to 4.8% of the supply. Two kinds of capital, on the same chain, give opposite answers.

Hoarding Ethereum up to 4.8% of the supply—and then seven years later, falling because of a single vulnerability. Security decides whether to stay or leave.

The report didn’t provide attack details or the loss figures. But choosing to shut down already tells you the story: the cost to patch and continue operating exceeds the value of seven years of brand accumulation. This isn’t this—this is a mature protocol admitting defeat after a security incident.

In today’s market environment, it forms a set of contradictions with another piece of news—contradictions that I haven’t yet seen anyone connect.

In the same hour, buying another 73 million dollars’ worth of Ethereum brings total holdings to 4.8% of circulating supply. Institutions keep gathering chips, while the protocol is exiting. On the surface it’s still “Ethereum,” but the two types of funds have completely different definitions of “security.” Institutions believe in the attack resistance of Ethereum’s consensus layer, but they lose out to every interaction at the application layer. This disagreement hasn’t been priced in yet.

If you look only at the buying cadence, it’s a signal of accelerating institutional demand. A 4.8% supply concentration is rare among major crypto assets. But there’s a transmission risk that’s easy to overlook: if the protocol’s shutdown triggers other protocols to proactively disclose their security status, or increases auditing thresholds, then the locked value in on-chain decentralized finance and the composable yield rate will face short-term pressure. These institutions won’t be forced to sell, but arbitrage capital that tracks trends will withdraw first, and on-chain liquidity will thin out by a layer.

On the geopolitical front, Iran’s missile strike on U.S. military bases has reversed the oil-price downtrend, and the crypto market has simultaneously entered a high-volatility window. This is the most likely external variable to interrupt Ethereum’s institutional buying cadence—not that they will sell, but that retail and quantitative traders’ Ethereum longs will passively reduce positions due to synchronized volatility with oil prices and Bitcoin, indirectly lowering the accounting-cost advantage.

If later we see: the attacker discloses attack details and the losses exceed 30% of its total locked holdings, then I will upgrade on-chain security from an isolated incident to a structural risk, and avoid all exposures to non-top-tier DeFi protocols in the short term. If, during any Ethereum price rebound, it starts to trim holdings—even by just 0.5%—I would conclude that institutions’ pricing logic for Ethereum has shifted.

The real thing that needs to be verified is the third point: whether a second protocol also proactively disclosed security issues after. Without a second “echo,” the protocol’s purchase still remains the most convincing action on this chain—but not everyone is at the same table.

📰 The Fed presses the pause button on rate hikes! Is the BTC $63,711 dip-buying window still open?

Event overview

To put it simply, it’s one thing: there are divisions within the Fed over raising rates. Some policymakers directly resisted the move to do a “one-time increase.” The meaning is clear—not to keep tightening, but to lean toward standing pat. This is a signal for the entire risk-asset market: the most hawkish moment may already be behind us. BTC is currently at $63,711.99, down 1.94% over the past 24 hours; ETH is worse, at $1,908.91, down 1.70%. But once this news hits, sentiment may reverse.

In-depth analysis

Why is this news important?

Folks, you need to get one thing straight: the Fed’s interest-rate policy is the core pricing anchor for the crypto market. Rate hikes = liquidity tightening = pressure on coin prices; rate cuts or standing pat = liquidity loosening = risk assets take off.

The key phrase here is “resist one time increase”—even a one-time rate hike is being resisted, which indicates that the Fed’s dovish voices are gaining strength. This isn’t a debate about whether to hike significantly; it’s a stance of “don’t even touch rates.”

Why might this shift be happening? The fundamental reason is that economic data can’t hold up. Inflation is easing, but the jobs market and consumer data are starting to soften. Another rate hike would be like pushing the economy toward a cliff. Policymakers haven’t suddenly turned lenient—they’ve been forced to pivot.

Viewed in the context of the cycle, this is actually very similar to the market’s expectations at the end of 2023 that the “rate-hike cycle has peaked.” Back then, the market rebounded from the bottom, with BTC rallying from around $25K to above $40K. Now the situation is more subtle—if even a “one-time increase” is rejected, the market will quickly price in rate-cut expectations, which is a real positive for BTC and ETH.

Connect it to recent developments: earlier CPI cooled down and employment data came in below expectations, effectively giving the market a warning. This news is confirmation, not a surprise. Smart money started positioning last week.

Impact on the market

In the short term, this news will directly boost sentiment. BTC at around $63,711—if buy pressure follows through, a short-term rebound to above $65K is completely reasonable. ETH at $1,908 is already oversold; once BTC stabilizes, ETH’s upside elasticity should be higher, and there’s a decent catch-up space.

The medium-term logic is worth paying closer attention to. If the Fed really holds steady, it would mean the peak in real interest rates, a weaker dollar, and institutional funds flowing back into risk assets. Buying power through the ETF channel should strengthen—those institutional funds that were waiting under tightening expectations will treat this as an entry signal.

Historically, you can look at January 2019. After the Fed clearly signaled “patience,” BTC rose from around $3,500 to above $4,000 within three months, for a gain of over 14%. It was also a turning point from hawkish to dovish, with market sentiment flipping overnight.

That said, be honest: don’t go all-in just because it’s good news. BTC fell nearly 2% in 24 hours, and ETH is down 1.7%, suggesting the market hasn’t fully digested the news yet. If it runs up too fast in the short term, profit-taking could hit near $65K. The real confirmation signal is whether BTC can hold above $65K and whether trading volume expands.

Trading ideas

- Coin: BTC / ETH
- Direction: Bullish 📈 Predicts a rise
- Duration: BTC 12 hours / ETH 24 hours

💡 My view is very clear: this is a short-term long setup window. BTC around $63,711 is a decent entry zone, with a stop loss below $62,500. First target $65,000; after a breakout, look for $67,000. 📰 美联储按下加息暂停键！BTC $63,711抄底窗口还开着吗

事件概述

说白了就一件事：美联储内部对加息产生了分歧，有政策制定者直接抵制"一次性加息"的操作。意思很明确——不是继续紧缩，而是倾向于按兵不动。这对整个风险资产市场是个信号：最鹰的时刻可能已经过去了。BTC现在报$63,711.99，24小时跌了1.94%；ETH更惨，$1,908.91，跌1.70%。但这条消息出来后，情绪面可能要逆转。

深度解读

为什么这条新闻重要？

老铁们得搞清楚一件事：美联储的利率政策是加密市场最核心的定价锚。加息=流动性收紧=币价承压，降息或按兵不动=流动性宽松=风险资产起飞。

这次的关键词是"resist one time increase"——连一次性加息都被抵制，说明美联储内部鸽派声音在变强。不是"要不要大幅加息"的争论，而是"连碰一下利率都别碰"的态度。

为什么会出现这种转变？根本原因还是经济数据撑不住了。通胀虽然在回落，但就业市场和消费数据开始走软，再加息等于把经济往悬崖上推。政策制定者不是突然变慈悲了，是被迫转向。

放到周期里看，这其实和2023年底那波"加息周期见顶"的预期非常类似。当时市场从底部反弹，BTC从$25K附近一路拉到$40K以上。现在的情况更微妙——如果连"一次性加息"都被否决，市场会迅速price in降息预期，这对BTC和ETH是实打实的利好。

和近期事件关联一下：此前CPI数据降温、就业数据不及预期，已经给市场打了预防针。这条新闻是confirmation，不是surprise。聪明钱上周就开始布局了。

对市场的影响

短期来看，这条消息会直接提振情绪。BTC从$63,711这个位置，如果买盘跟上，短期反弹到$65K上方完全合理。ETH在$1,908这个位置已经超卖了，一旦BTC企稳，ETH弹性会更大，补涨空间不小。

中期逻辑更值得重视。美联储如果真的按住不动，意味着实际利率见顶，美元走弱，机构资金重新流入风险资产。ETF渠道的买入力会增强——之前在紧缩预期下观望的机构资金，会把这个当作入场信号。

历史上可以参考2019年1月，美联储明确释放"耐心"信号后，BTC在三个月内从$3,500涨到$4,000以上，涨幅超过14%。当时也是从鹰转鸽的拐点，市场情绪一夜反转。

但说句实话，别一看到利好就满仓冲。24小时BTC跌了快2%，ETH跌了1.7%，说明市场还没完全消化这条消息。如果短期拉得太快，$65K附近会有获利盘砸出来。真正的确认信号是看BTC能不能站稳$65K并且成交量放大。

【ETH is at a critical moment】

One seasoned veteran in the crypto world has been watching ETH’s chart, and honestly, it’s a bit unsettling.

At the position $ 1915, it’s stuck—neither up nor down. It can’t push higher, and it also won’t fall further. Trading volume is active, but the direction just can’t be chosen.

Looking at the data, there are three signals here:

First, ETH is ranging and consolidating: +0.2% over the past 24 hours, and -0.4% over the past 7 days. The window for direction selection is nearing, and the active volume indicates that capital is participating.

Second, the positive divergence signal is showing. The Fear & Greed Index is only 29, and the weekly average is also 29. Historical patterns tell me this level is worth paying attention to.

Third, the extremely undervalued zone. The ETH at $ 1915 is already down more than 60% compared with its previous historical highs, meaning an oversold range has formed.

With these three signals stacked together, I have to say this kind of combination isn’t common. From $ 1825 to $ 1963, the potential isn’t huge, but it’s not small either. I lean bullish, but I won’t call trades—after this range consolidation, the probability of an upside move is higher.

My strategy is simple: if it can hold $ 1825, then look for $ 1963 and even higher. If it breaks down, I’ll admit defeat and exit. Setting a stop-loss is the most rational thing I can do.

Next week I’ll publish the results. Everyone, do you think this wave in ETH can truly move upward?

【ETH到了关键时刻】

币圈老炮一枚，盯着ETH这走势，说实话有点烦躁。

$ 1915这个位置不上不下，涨不上去，跌也跌不下来。成交量倒是活跃，但方向就是选不出来。

看数据，三个信号摆在这：

第一，ETH震荡整理，24小时+0.2%，7日-0.4%，方向选择临近，成交量活跃说明资金在参与。

第二，积极背离信号，恐惧贪婪指数只有29，周均值也是29，历史规律告诉我这个位置值得重视。

第三，极低估值区，$ 1915的ETH相比历史高点跌幅已经超过60%，超跌区间已经形成。

三个信号叠加，说真的，这种组合不常见。从$ 1825到$ 1963的空间，说大不大说小不小。我倾向于看涨，但不会喊单——这个区间震荡后向上的概率更大。

我的策略很简单：如果能守住$ 1825，看$ 1963甚至更高；跌破就认输离场。设置好止损，这是我能做的最理性的事。

下周我会公开结果。各位，你们觉得ETH这波能真往上走吗？
